preparation: Provide legible current broad physical-region reference views and accurately located Lake Nipissing/Nipissing First Nation and Niagara cases. Keep each community/provider area distinct from its broad physical region.

Provide concise own-word attributed factual activity cards from the reviewed accounts, including actual fisheries/forestry/business activity and tourism/visitor services/maintenance. Include actual recreational visits/park uses as well as paid visitor-service jobs.
actions: Identify the selected Canadian Shield and Great Lakes–StLawrence Lowlands reference areas, then describe several supported human activities within them, including industrial/resource or service work AND recreation. Locate the actual selected cases; one employer is not the whole region.

Distinguish the activity people do at a place from a job serving it: a recreational visitor and a tourism worker can use the same place differently. Describe actual land/water purposes and needs/wants served.

Explain why these are significant documented examples without inventing a statistical ranking or assuming the headline landscape determines everyone’s work. Identify an unsupported activity label on a fresh supplied account and ask what actual-use evidence would resolve it.

Retain complete shared-claim checks separately: describe at least five jobs/what people do, earning-money/community benefits and an interest-to-job connection; distinguish the full land/water purpose range, including conservation/unbuilt and a mixed-use case, using accurately supplied examples. These checks do not make every example a Canadian regional fact.
physical-region-activities.positive: Accurate located human-activity examples in more than one physical region, including industrial/service work and recreation, with work/use distinctions and provider limits.
nearMiss: Lists physical features but no human activities.
Names only tourism jobs but never recreational activity.
Turns one provider’s workforce into regional employment shares.
physical-region-activities.transfer: Describe activities in a new accurate regional account, separating supported significant examples from invented statistics and appearance-only uses.

preparation: Provide a current political map locating Ontario and the Northwest Territories and the attributed Fort William/Tuktuuyaqtuuq source cards, keeping actual community and dated voices explicit.
Use source-supported work/education/transport and harvesting/tourism/housing/erosion-monitoring examples. Do not infer every household’s experience from a provider programme.
actions: For each selected political-region case, describe a significant opportunity and challenge from the actual sources and explain how it can affect everyday life: Ontario education/transport work and stated recruitment/support needs; Northwest Territories harvesting/tourism opportunities and documented coastal erosion/relocation challenges.

Connect the actual activity and housing/food/transport land/water uses with needs/wants and community benefits. Distinguish paid work, community harvesting and voluntary participation where the sources do; do not assume all work is paid or all residents share one role.

Describe a source-supported response, such as educational transport/support or coastal monitoring/relocation, without claiming an unmeasured universal successful outcome. This description does not certify B1.3’s separate industries+citizens effectiveness duty.

Compare the two cases with explicit source/date/place limits. On a fresh accurate Canadian regional card, identify an opportunity/challenge and say which missing evidence prevents a stronger claim. Retain the full shared job/use checks from the activities protocol.
regional-quality-of-life.positive: Describes supported quality-of-life opportunities and challenges in selected Canadian political regions and relates them to everyday work/education, food, housing or transport, without stereotyping residents.
nearMiss: Gives only a job list without its opportunities/challenges for daily life.
Calls all members poor because one cost-support programme exists.
Claims coastal monitoring alone proves erosion or relocation problems are solved.
regional-quality-of-life.transfer: Use a new accurately attributed region/account to distinguish a supported opportunity or challenge from a universal resident stereotype.
